ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the center of the figure is a rectangular functional block, internally labeled “TG”. On the left there is an input terminal labeled “A”, on the right there is an output terminal labeled “Y”, and the signal path goes from A through TG to Y. There is one control terminal above and below the rectangle respectively; beside the upper control terminal it is labeled “0”, and a small bubble is drawn where it enters TG, indicating inverted/complementary control; beside the lower control terminal it is labeled “1”. Reasoning: In digital circuit symbols, a switch block labeled TG and with upper and lower complementary control terminals represents a transmission gate; this type of transmission gate is usually composed of complementary NMOS and PMOS, so it is a CMOS transmission gate.

planner_metadata.knowledge_role: Use the electronics convention that “TG” denotes a transmission gate, and that a CMOS transmission gate is controlled by complementary signals applied to parallel NMOS/PMOS devices; the bubble marks the active-low/complementary control. A bidirectional A-to-Y pass element with complementary controls is therefore a CMOS transmission gate.
